newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says Griffin oil output cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says Griffin oil output cut.

text.p: Oil production has been cut at the Griffin oil field offshore of Western Australia due to failure of a remotely operated well on a floating production facility, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Friday.

"A remotely operated well head has failed," a BHP spokesman told Reuters. He would not say how much production had been cut by. The facility was shut down for scheduled maintenance work on April 19, at which time it was producing an average daily rate of 50,000 bpd, although capacity is closer to 80,000 bpd.
Griffin came back on stream on July 3 and production was being ramped up when the probelm was identified, the spokesman said.
The field is operated by BHP, which holds a 45-percent stake in the consortium. Mobil Corp of the United States holds 35 percent and Inpex Alpha Ltd the remaining 20 percent.
The spokesman said the problem with the remote system was being investigated and that it was too early to say when the unit will be repaired.
"We cannot precisely say when the problem will be fixed," the spokesman said.
A source familiar with the project said the facility was producing " well under 50,000 barrels ( a day)," although BHP would not confirm the figure.
